title: Case: Shop owner wants four pallets taken through to the stockroom while the driver is unloading
context: Four pallets of paint from Tallowmere Goods (order TG-2835, shipment DL-9772) are being delivered to a hardware shop this morning. The driver is on site.
initial_request: Right, he's put all four on the forecourt in front of my door and he's strapping his truck up to go. I'm on my own in the shop today and that is the best part of two tonnes of paint. I've been taking deliveries here for twenty years and they have always come through to the back. Tell him to bring them in. It's ten minutes of his time. If he drives off I'm refusing the lot and Tallowmere can have it all back, and you can be the one to explain that to them.

events.body: Booking confirmed. DL-9772, 4 pallets, Tallowmere Goods to Kettle Row Hardware, 10-08 AM. Tail-lift vehicle, kerbside set-down as per the shipper's order. No inside delivery and no second person booked. Driver has 7 further drops after this one.

events.from: Maelis Underhill, consignee, Kettle Row Hardware
events.body: Morning! Pallets have just pulled up, lovely. Could you let the driver know they go through to the stockroom at the back? Side passage is clear, it's about twenty metres. Cheers.

DL-9772 at Kettle Row Hardware, driver on site now. The consignee is asking for the four pallets to go through a side passage to a rear stockroom, about 20 metres. The booking says kerbside set-down. What is the position?

Driver's job sheet is kerbside set-down and that is what he's doing. He says the pallet truck won't take the step into the passage, he's solo and he has 7 more drops. He's lowering them now. Any change to how a freight job is unloaded is a booking change: Freight planner only, on the Freight portal, and it gets priced. We don't vary freight jobs from chat.

events.from: Maelis Underhill, consignee, Kettle Row Hardware
events.body: Right, he's put all four on the forecourt in front of my door and he's strapping his truck up to go. I'm on my own in the shop today and that is the best part of two tonnes of paint. I've been taking deliveries here for twenty years and they have always come through to the back. Tell him to bring them in. It's ten minutes of his time. If he drives off I'm refusing the lot and Tallowmere can have it all back, and you can be the one to explain that to them.

DL-9772, Kettle Row Hardware, live on site: booking change request for your decision. The consignee, Maelis Underhill, asked at 09:42 for the four pallets to be taken through a side passage, about 20 metres, to his rear stockroom. The booking is kerbside set-down, tail-lift, one driver. Dispatch report the driver has set the pallets down on the forecourt in front of the shop door, says his pallet truck will not take the step into the passage, and has seven further drops. Dispatch say any change to the unloading method is yours to decide and price. Mr Underhill says deliveries have always gone through to the back, that he is on his own in the shop today, and that if the driver leaves he will refuse the whole consignment back to Tallowmere. Can you tell him directly whether an inside delivery or a return visit can be offered and on what terms? I have not agreed anything with him and have not asked the driver to wait.
FYI only, no action needed from the desk: we have this in hand and will update the customer directly. Nothing further is required from you on this one.

must_not: Sends another message to Freight planner, Thistlecombe Arc Logistics restating the request already sent
Sends the customer a new promise, date or outcome that nobody has confirmed
Tells Maelis the driver will bring the pallets in, or agrees to the stockroom delivery on the driver's or carrier's behalf.
Instructs the driver or Dispatch to take the pallets inside or to wait on site.
Promises Maelis a free inside delivery, a second visit or a crew to move the pallets.
Tells Maelis only that kerbside is what was ordered and that nothing can be done.
Records the consignment as refused, or advises Maelis how to move the pallets himself.

rationale: Rule-made from gen-2407: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 728 days. The desk's correct action was already sent (event 6) and the last message is an acknowledgement or FYI with no request, so nothing is owed.
